title: Custom Indexing for Nanopore Sequencing Platform
author: Mrinalini Watsa
materials: GoTaq Green Master Mix Promega Catalog #M7122

steps.title: Design PCR1 primers with overhangs
steps.instruction: Design gene‑specific primers that carry a 5′ overhang compatible with either Illumina (TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG forward, GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACA reverse) or Oxford Nanopore (TTTCTGTTGGTGCTGATATTGC forward, ACTTGCCTGTCGCTCTATCTTC reverse) chemistry. The overhang will be incorporated in the PCR1 product.

steps.title: Perform PCR1 with overhang primers
steps.instruction: Run PCR1 using the overhang‑containing primers under the same cycling conditions as a standard gene‑specific PCR; the overhang does not affect chemistry. The amplified product will be 45–60 bp longer than the native amplicon because of the added overhangs on each end.

steps.title: Order 96‑well indexing primer plates
steps.instruction: Order 96 forward and 96 reverse custom indexing primers (Illumina‑OVH or ONT‑OVH) in a 96‑well plate format using the provided Excel files (e.g., ONT‑ILL_overhang_FwPlate_VerticalConfig.xlsx).

steps.title: Dilute PCR1 products 1:10
steps.instruction: In a clean tube or fresh 96‑well plate add 18 µL nuclease‑free water then 2 µL of each PCR1 product to obtain a 20 µL 1:10 dilution for every sample.

steps.title: Prepare indexing master mix for 96 reactions
steps.instruction: For a 15 µL reaction per well (96 wells + 10 % extra buffer) assemble the following per reaction: 2 µL diluted template DNA, 2.4 µL indexing primer (from the plate), 10.6 µL master‑mix cocktail (GoTaq Green + water). For the full plate the cocktail consists of 7.5 µL GoTaq Green and 4.3 µL nuclease‑free water per reaction (total 792 µL GoTaq, 454.1 µL water). Mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Spin down lyophilized plates
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge both the PCR‑product plate and the indexing‑primer plate to collect any lyophilized material at the bottom of the wells.

steps.title: Reconstitute each oligo to 100 µM
steps.instruction: Refer to the oligo documentation; add nuclease‑free water to each lyophilized oligo so that the final concentration is 100 µM. Example: if the well contains 25 nmol, add 250 µL water to reach 100 µM.

steps.title: Create 1:20 dilution to 1.25 µM
steps.instruction: From the interim 25 µM indexing plate, dilute each well 1:20 (e.g., 5 µL stock + 95 µL water) to obtain a 1.25 µM indexing primer plate.

steps.title: Combine forward and reverse primers
steps.instruction: In a new plate add 50 µL of the forward primer and 50 µL of the matching reverse primer to the same well (e.g., Index 1 forward in A1 with Index 1 reverse in A1). Mix by pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Add water to make 25 µM interim plate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL nuclease‑free water to each well of the combined‑primer plate, mix. The volume becomes 200 µL per well, giving a 1:4 dilution and a final primer concentration of 25 µM.

steps.title: Transfer 5 µL to new plate
steps.instruction: Pipette 5 µL from each well of the 25 µM interim plate into a fresh plate.

steps.title: Make final 1.25 µM indexing plate
steps.instruction: Add 95 µL nuclease‑free water to each well containing the 5 µL transfer, mix. Total volume 100 µL per well, final primer concentration 1.25 µM. Seal with piercable aluminum seals, wipe the surface, store at –20 °C. Never peel off the seal; reseal with a fresh seal after each use.

steps.title: Mix diluted PCR product
steps.instruction: Gently pipette up and down (or pulse‑vortex 5 s) the 1:10 diluted PCR product, then spin down. This creates the template for the indexing PCR.

steps.title: Assess PCR1 product on gel
steps.instruction: Run an aliquot of the PCR1 product on an agarose gel. If only the expected band is present, proceed. If primer dimers or non‑specific bands appear, perform a bead‑based cleanup, re‑run a few samples on a gel to confirm cleanup, then continue.

steps.title: Set up indexing PCR controls
steps.instruction: Include at least one negative control (water instead of template with its assigned index) and one positive control (PCR1 product with its assigned index) in the indexing PCR plate.

steps.title: Run indexing PCR
steps.instruction: Thermal profile: 95 °C 3 min initial denaturation; 15 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 55 °C 15 s, 72 °C 40 s; 72 °C 1 min final extension; hold at 10 °C indefinitely. Adjust extension time by adding ~1 min per additional 1000 bp of target length.

steps.title: Optional: Index >96 samples
steps.instruction: For more than 96 samples, after the first indexing plate perform a second round of dual indexing using ONT Native Barcodes (NBD114.24 for up to 2 304 samples or NBD114.96 for up to 9 216 samples) according to the ONT kit instructions.

steps.title: Normalize indexed amplicons – fluorometry
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration of each indexing PCR product with a fluorometer (e.g., Qubit). Normalize all samples to the same molarity and pool them equimolarly.

steps.title: Normalize indexed amplicons – gel brightness
steps.instruction: Run 1.5–2 % agarose gels with a suitable ladder. Photograph the gel, rank band intensity (strong, intermediate, weak). Transfer 3 µL of strong, 6 µL of intermediate, and 8 µL of weak bands to the pool. Include negative‑control blanks as weak bands.

steps.title: Pool samples and perform bead cleanup if needed
steps.instruction: Combine the normalized 96‑sample pool (typically >100 µL). Take 3 µL and run on a gel to check for primer dimers. If the pool is clean and ≥200 fmol, proceed to ONT ligation. If dimers are present or DNA is too dilute, perform a bead cleanup on half the pool: choose a bead‑to‑sample ratio appropriate for the amplicon size, elute into ~30 µL, dilute 1:10 (1 µL eluate + 9 µL water), run 2 µL on a gel to confirm cleanup, quantify, and multiply by 10 to obtain the original concentration. If DNA is still insufficient, repeat cleanup on the remaining half.

steps.title: Follow ONT NBD114 ligation protocol
steps.instruction: Using the cleaned, equimolar pool, execute the Oxford Nanopore Native Barcoding Kit (114.24 or 114.96) ligation protocol as described on the Nanopore Community website. Verify pool quality before loading the flow cell.
